account:
Today has mostly followed ordinary routines. I read my appointments, made the ten o'clock market walk, and am now home for the noon lunch engagement. Accounts at the town hall are due at thirteen hundred. The neighbour confirmed that tea at fifteen hundred is at the cottage at (16, -60, 105), just east of the ferry landing; the original appointment lacked those details, but that uncertainty is now resolved.

The main unusual report is that the builder called for the innkeeper near the inn around 09:34 and requested a private meeting. Townsfolk 30 and 20 both repeated that call, although they may simply be repeating the same event rather than independent information. I heard the distant shout myself but could not understand it. Later I saw the builder walking with a lantern near the plaza, and the innkeeper crossing the plaza carrying an emerald. At 11:18 I heard another distant builder shout without understanding its words. I have not witnessed a private meeting or learned its subject. My attempted greeting to the innkeeper did not reach them, so I have no reply from them.

Residents also reported the baker carrying wheat at the bakery, which seems consistent with ordinary baking. The secretary said no correspondence or reports of unusual business had arrived. Her initial request for my engagements despite the existing appointment book was confusing, but she subsequently consulted and preserved the book; I have no evidence of concealment.

The builder's wish for privacy is worth a discreet, ordinary conversation with the builder or innkeeper, but it is not evidence of wrongdoing. The meeting could concern building work, trade, or a personal matter; I do not yet know its purpose. I should keep my scheduled appointments and seek firsthand information without spreading suspicion.
